task_specification.objective: Repair the ordinary release surface by restoring authored cemetery spatial integrity and the upgrade-choice presentation, then preserve or minimally harden the existing dense-profile handoff for host recapture without claiming native qualification.

diagnosis.root_cause: The active release defect is a west-perimeter presentation failure: the authored map, outer datum, and shipped-camera visibility contract do not provide reliable external depth. Deferred evidence also indicates landmark visibility and native dense qualification still need host retesting, but the candidate already contains editor-only dense metrics and cannot prove native performance on the live software renderer.

stop_conditions: Keep AuthoredCemeteryPackage as one intact authoritative map instance; do not split, duplicate, surgically edit, or replace imported child meshes.
Do not repeat dense gameplay tuning or fabricate native-renderer evidence; if the existing dense contract is already complete, preserve it and leave the native dependency explicit.
Do not claim issue closure, phase-gate passage, runtime screenshots, or native performance qualification; GameLoop Runtime and Tester own those verdicts.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different strategy from prior transform tuning: repair the world through a single authored-package/outer-datum binding and isolated camera-visibility contract, while implementing the real upgrade-choice visual hierarchy as the ordinary player-facing increment. Treat dense work as a receipt/handoff audit only, not another performance-tuning treatment.

runtime: GameLoop Runtime/Tester must boot the candidate and recapture spawn, critical route/objective, and four cardinal first-person views from an interior native street, plus before/near-contact/after-departure landmark traversal.

Perform real horizontal and vertical mouse-motion probes and ordinary movement replay; verify yaw/camera_forward and pitch changes, larger traversable scale, external depth, central building/landmark visibility, collision, perimeter boundary, and absence of disappearance or occlusion drift.
